title: Completed shriek composition laws
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the specified six operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Finite inputs used for compact support carry compatible etale-origin witnesses; integral inputs are derived complete with compatible witnessed finite reductions, rational operations are raw localization, and algebraically closed coefficients are represented at a common finite coefficient field. All operations below are restricted to their stated constructible domains; tensor factors and comparisons have their stated finite-Tor hypotheses. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow hW$ be separated finite-type morphisms of finite-type $k$-schemes. Choose compatible compactification towers and common refining towers as in [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. For a compactification $f=pj$, with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper, put $F_f=S_pJ_j$; write $g=qi$ similarly. On normalized strict semilinear coefficient systems, write $S_p$ for proper derived direct image and $J_j$ for open extension. Define $a_{g,f}:F_gF_f\to F_{gf}$ by replacing the adjacent $J_iS_p$ in $S_qJ_iS_pJ_j$ by its normalized proper/open interchange, followed by proper and open compositors. For all normalized inputs whose levels and every intermediate expression have common finite cohomology and Tor intervals, the resulting maps are independent of the compatible tower, intertwine refinement comparisons, satisfy both unit laws, and satisfy
$$a_{h,gf}\circ(F_h a_{g,f})=a_{hg,f}\circ(a_{h,g}F_f).$$
Here refinement squares include the commutative noncartesian intermediate proper/open squares, with their normalized clopen-projection comparisons. The equalities are equalities of derived system maps before evaluation. The natural realization isomorphisms $c_V:R\lim V(\mathcal R K)\cong V_{\mathrm{int}}(K)$ carry these maps, also inside nested functors, to the specified completed integral compact-support compositors and preserve the displayed equations and refinement compatibility. For bounded constructible integral inputs these expressions meet the required uniform finite-Tor bounds locally: on finite affine covers and their inverse images the separated finite-type preservation bounds apply, with the minimum lower and maximum upper endpoints giving global intervals. Thus the integral equations hold without assuming the schemes separated over $k$. Raw rationalization and common finite-field scalar transport carry these equations to the corresponding field-coefficient compositors. The finite-coefficient compositors are the unital associative ones of [thm-sf-comp-composition].

proof.text: Use [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting] in its semilinear setting (b), with the supplied Realizations interface. This provides the specified proper/open map and the proper and open compositors in the derived system categories themselves. The theorem systemProperOpenGammaIsIso of [lem-sf-system-proper-open-support] proves invertibility of this actual map on arbitrary systems by the supported-counit argument. For a compatible tower $Y\hookrightarrow\bar Y\to Z$, $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to\bar Y$, put $U=\bar X\times_{\bar Y}Y$. Whisker the proper/open map for this square on both sides, then compose the open and proper compositors and their named-composite equality transports. This is exactly completedShriekA. All these factors are invertible; typeclass composition proves completedShriekComposition_isIso, without finite evaluation, an isomorphism-detection argument, or any additional bounds. Identification with the specified finite comparison is the separate task in step 5.

proof.text: For completedShriekRefinementLaws, first take right-adjoint mates of the proved normalized pullback associativity theorem [lem-sf-integral-system-compositor-associativity], retaining equality transports for chosen composite arrows. Insert the identity-pair normalization [lem-sf-system-push-identity-pair] into the vertical equation of the supplied ProperOpenCoherence package. Naturality moves the inverse proper-image identity past the second gamma, and adjacent inverse compositor factors cancel. This proves the open refinement composition equation. Apply the outer proper image, use proper compositor associativity and naturality, and obtain R_(r.comp s)=R_s R_r. Every R_r is invertible on arbitrary system inputs by [lem-sf-system-proper-open-support]. Applying the composition equation to id.comp id gives an invertible idempotent, hence the identity. For parallel r,s out of c, use the dense compactification inf(c,c) and its first projection t. Density makes t.comp r=t.comp s by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]. The composition equation and cancellation of the invertible R_t give equality. These arguments use no additional Good bounds. The remaining choice-independence proof uses inf(e,e′), composition, density and the same arbitrary-input invertibility, as in the existing Lean proof. All equations are proved before finite evaluation.

proof.text:
Consider refining compatible pair towers indexed by $1\to2$, with the proper arrows $w:U_1\to U_2$, $v:\bar X_1\to\bar X_2$, $u:\bar Y_1\to\bar Y_2$ of [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. Label the proper/open squares $A=(X,U_1;X,U_2)$, $B=(U_2,\bar X_2;Y,\bar Y_2)$, $C=(U_1,\bar X_1;Y,\bar Y_1)$, $D=(Y,\bar Y_1;Y,\bar Y_2)$, $E=(X,\bar X_1;X,\bar X_2)$ and $F=(U_1,\bar X_1;U_2,\bar X_2)$, listing top then bottom rows. All are commutative; only the tower squares $B,C$ must be cartesian. Horizontal pasting gives $\Gamma_E=\Gamma_F\Gamma_A$; the two vertical pastings of the same outer square give $\Gamma_C\Gamma_D=\Gamma_F\Gamma_B$, by [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting]. Insert the canonical compositors throughout. Naturality permits the disjoint occurrences $\Gamma_A,\Gamma_B$ to pass each other. Substitution therefore gives
$$R_{gf}\,a_2=a_1\,(R_gF_f^{1})\,(F_g^{2}R_f):F_g^{2}F_f^{2}\longrightarrow F_{gf}^{1}.$$
Here $R_f,R_g,R_{gf}$ are step 2's reverse refinement maps. Inverting them gives the asserted forward refinement square. Together with common refinement and the cocycle, this proves tower independence of the composition maps. Lean assembly: retain named-composite equality transports. Derive the proper-image right unitor from [lem-sf-integral-system-compositor-associativity] applied to (f,id,id) and the two-identity normalization [lem-sf-system-push-identity-pair], cancelling the invertible compositor and identity comparison. Apply one horizontal and two vertical pasting equations to the A--F diagram, move the identity comparison by naturality, and cancel the final proper compositor. This is the componentwise refinement calculation already used in StrictTowerCompositionPasting, specialized directly to the specified semilinear maps; no finite evaluation or additional cartesian face is required. For compilation the categorical calculation is parameterized by a private product bundle of comparison maps for fixed categories and functors, with a separate record of proved/supplied laws, then instantiated with Operations and Realizations; no concrete derived-site definition is unfolded during the internal naturality calculation.

proof.text: Choose successive compactifications $Z\hookrightarrow\bar Z\to W$, $Y\hookrightarrow\bar Y\to\bar Z$, $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to\bar Y$; the compatible-tower lemma [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] supplies their intermediate opens and common refinements. Set $T=\bar Y\times_{\bar Z}Z$, $V=\bar X\times_{\bar Y}T$, $U=\bar X\times_{\bar Y}Y$. There are proper/open squares $A=(U,V;Y,T)$, $B=(V,\bar X;T,\bar Y)$ and $C=(T,\bar Y;Z,\bar Z)$. Applying [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting], the horizontal rectangle has $\Gamma_{A+B}=\Gamma_B\Gamma_A$ and the vertical rectangle has $\Gamma_{B+C}=\Gamma_B\Gamma_C$, with whiskers/compositors inserted. The two compact-support composites become respectively $\Gamma_B\Gamma_A\Gamma_C$ and $\Gamma_B\Gamma_C\Gamma_A$. The disjoint occurrences $A,C$ commute by naturality: componentwise this is the equation $G'(v)\,\alpha_M=\alpha_N\,G(v)$ for a natural transformation $\alpha:G\to G'$ and the other component map $v:M\to N$. Hence the two composites agree. Associativity of the proper and open compositors removes the intermediate parentheses, giving the displayed equation of the item. Step 3 carries it to any other compatible tower. This proof takes place before evaluation.

proof.text: For an identity morphism choose its compactification with both arrows identities. The resulting interchange square has identity horizontal or vertical arrows, so its $\Gamma$ is the identity by [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting]. The remaining arrows are exactly its unital proper and open compositors. Thus $a_{g,1}$ and $a_{1,f}$ are the canonical unit maps, and step 3 proves the same assertion for any supplied compactification. At each fixed finite coefficient stage, the evaluated proper/open map is the finite one by [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting]; the evaluated compositors are the canonical adjunction compositors. The construction is consequently the compactification construction whose unital associative finite law is [thm-sf-comp-composition], on precisely its bounded-below witnessed domain.

proof.text:
Now take integral inputs satisfying the intermediate-domain conditions. Apply [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] to each source word $V$, target word $V'$ and structural arrow $\tau:V\to V'$. It identifies the specified integral arrow with
$$\tau_{\rm int}=c_{V'}\,\mathcal L(\tau_{\mathcal R K})\,c_V^{-1}.$$
This applies also to arrows inside nested functors, not just to a single evaluated compact-support object. In any composite, the adjacent factors $c_V^{-1}c_V$ cancel; $\mathcal L$ preserves compositions and identities. Thus the system equations of steps 2--5 become the integral refinement, unit and associativity equations, for the specified integral compositors. The same cancellation gives equality for any two refining towers. In particular, no inference of equality of integral maps from finite reductions, and no choice of lifts of finite-level arrows, enters the argument.

proof.text: For every integral constructible input, apply [lem-sf-constructible-reduction-good] to obtain Good for the actual reduction system, with its normalization, common bounds and retained compatible origins. This includes inputs not occurring in the expression and requires no geometric hypothesis on those unused inputs. Induct on the support expression. At a variable the domain and integral constructibility are the input hypotheses. A pullback or tensor case contradicts isSupportWord. At a proper constructor apply [lem-sf-proper-support-step-bounds] to the root Good property of the induction hypothesis and to the integral constructibility of its evaluation. At an open constructor use [lem-sf-open-support-step-bounds] in the same way. Combine the resulting root Good fact with the recursive admissibility hypothesis.

At a compact-support constructor use its specified ambient compactification over the original base. Its proper map and the finite-type target show that the ambient scheme is finite type; its open is quasi-compact since the compactified morphism is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-sf-open-support-step-bounds] to the actual open, then [lem-sf-proper-support-step-bounds] to the actual proper arrow. Store both resulting Good facts, including the intermediate open output, alongside the inductive admissibility of the inner expression. The two integral preservation conclusions give integral constructibility of the compact-support evaluation. Finally pair the input-domain conjunction with the inductively assembled admissibility. This completes completedShriekIntegralBounds with no new hypothesis on structural separatedness. Other original open obligations retain the remaining proof steps of this node.

Finally use the raw scalar localization of [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization], with $R=S=\mathcal O_E$, $\phi$ the identity and $t=u$ the uniformizer, for the supplied integral operations and natural transformations; it extends exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functors and their natural transformations and preserves identities, vertical composition and whiskering. Each integral equation becomes the same equation on the same objects with every component tensored with $1$; composition of fractions is $(v/t^b)(u/t^a)=vu/t^{a+b}$, so the naturality and whiskering equations persist on all rational morphisms as well. These are the specified rational compact-support operations of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For algebraically closed coefficients, represent the finite collection of inputs and arrows in each diagram over one common finite coefficient field, as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Apply the integral and rational argument at that field and then its functor to the common-stage category. This sends each identity/composite to the identity/composite of its images; hence the two sides remain equal, including refinements and nested maps. On passing to any further common field, the same scalar-extension functor again sends that already established equation to an equation. This proves precisely the asserted transport of the laws to the specified field-coefficient compositors, without a Karoubi envelope.
